comparison: Both support the core finding of polysaccharide-induced phage production and bacterial growth promotion. OpenEval focuses on phylogenetic identification (C27-C30), while peer review emphasizes the broader claim about phage augmentation of polysaccharide use (C3, C28-C32, C54, C63-C64). Both find evidence solid.

Both support transcriptomic findings. OpenEval evaluates differential expression data (C31-C32) with qRT-PCR validation as strong support. Peer review includes these claims (C31-C32) within the broader acceptance of the manuscript's primary findings about polysaccharide use.

Both support the novelty claims (C63-C64). OpenEval notes appropriate contextualization with citations but cautions about 'first report' claims. Peer review accepts these claims as part of the overall solid evidence for the manuscript's primary findings.

Both support TEM observations of phage morphology and induction. OpenEval evaluates phage characterization (C33-C38) with controls for contamination. Peer review accepts chronic infection evidence (C33-C35) with only minor reservations about mechanism.

Both support chronic infection interpretation. OpenEval finds extrusion/budding structures (C39-C41) reasonable with literature support but notes lack of direct functional validation. Peer review accepts chronic infection evidence (C39, C41) with minor mechanistic weaknesses noted.

Both support evidence of non-lytic infection. OpenEval evaluates growth curves and cell integrity data (C42-C49) as well-supported but notes 'healthy' claim needs additional viability assays. Peer review accepts chronic infection evidence (C42-C44) as solid and convincing.

Strong agreement on dose-response and time-course data. OpenEval finds quantitative phage counts (C45-C49) well-supported with appropriate controls. Peer review specifically acknowledges differential phage proliferation assays as convincing evidence.

Both support parallel findings in strain zth2. OpenEval evaluates growth, transcriptomics, and TEM data (C54-C59) as supporting generalizability. Peer review accepts these observations (C57-C59) as part of the chronic infection evidence.

Strong agreement on secretion system upregulation. OpenEval finds transcriptomic data (C60-C62) well-documented but notes lack of direct functional evidence. Peer review accepts differential gene expression analyses and does not challenge the speculative framing of mechanistic interpretation.

Both support bacterial strain characterization. OpenEval evaluates phylogenetic analysis and taxonomic proposal (C50-C53) as following standard practice. Peer review accepts the Lentisphaerae isolate characterization as valuable for understanding deep-sea microbial life.

Both support phage genome characterization. OpenEval finds sequencing and bioinformatic analysis (C65-C67) well-supported despite incomplete genomes. Peer review accepts genomic characterization without objection as part of study strengths.

Both support genome comparison findings. OpenEval evaluates prophage identification (C68-C69) as well-supported but notes C69 is speculative with limited sampling. Peer review accepts the genomic analyses (C68) as part of overall study strengths.

Both support phylogenetic classification. OpenEval finds terL-based analysis (C72) methodologically sound with appropriate bootstrap support. Peer review accepts phylogenetic analyses (C72) as part of the genomic characterization without objection.

Both support AMG identification but OpenEval notes lack of functional validation. OpenEval finds genome annotation (C73-C77) well-supported but emphasizes missing functional validation. Peer review acknowledges AMG identification (C73-C74) but notes mechanistic uncertainty and need for experiments on 'HOW' genes are used.

Strong agreement on uncertainty about metabolic reprogramming mechanism. Both rate claims as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes speculation without functional validation (C5, C80, C82). Peer review emphasizes need for mechanistic experiments and preliminary nature of evidence for AMG function.

Partial overlap on ExbB absence interpretation. OpenEval supports the observation (C77) that ExbB absence in host strengthens metabolic supplementation interpretation. Peer review rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting the 'selfishness' concept needs development and mechanistic distinction is unclear.

Strong agreement on uncertainty about selfishness hypothesis. Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval finds extrapolation to 'widespread' occurrence (C85, C88) highly speculative with insufficient sampling. Peer review notes the selfishness concept (C85) needs more development and current work doesn't clearly distinguish mechanisms.

Both express uncertainty about mutualism interpretation. OpenEval rates C81 as UNCERTAIN, noting circumstantial evidence without quantified fitness benefits. Peer review notes inability to distinguish whether phages help hosts grow or hijack mechanisms, representing a key mechanistic gap.
OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C1-C2, C6-C18) as appropriately cited literature support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory context claims.
OpenEval evaluates additional background claims (C19-C26) establishing knowledge gaps as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates background citations (C70-C71, C78-C79, C84) providing interpretive context as appropriately supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature context claims.
OpenEval evaluates methodological statement about sample collection (C83) as appropriately documented. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methods claim.
OpenEval evaluates citations to authors' recent work (C86-C87) as providing important context for broader patterns. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these cited findings.

Peer review accepts the overarching claim (C3) that phage isolates augment polysaccharide use as the manuscript's primary finding with solid evidence. OpenEval does not have a single result evaluating this integrative claim, though related claims are evaluated across multiple OpenEval results (R1, R2, R14).

Peer review accepts claim C4 about chronic infection as part of the phage characterization. OpenEval does not explicitly evaluate C4 as a standalone claim, though chronic infection evidence is evaluated in R3, R4, and R5.
